statusDetail: Atomic audit completed for all 58 registered checks across representative home, category, search, game, login, and recovery surfaces.

page.notes: Server-rendered game catalog with client hydration, embedded third-party game frames, a PWA manifest/service worker, and custom consent/login overlays.

principleOutcomes.reason: CrazyGames exposes public game discovery and play, but no declared agent-facing transaction/tool surface; emerging WebMCP capability is therefore treated as out of scope. No summarization, generation, or other inference task is part of the representative game browsing and play journey.

paths.description: Homepage and primary discovery surface; tested desktop, 360 px mobile, dark preference, reduced motion, forced colors, performance, security, memory, and no-JS rendering.
Action category listing representing catalog/index templates and breadcrumb/filter navigation.
Search results journey at a narrow viewport, representing query and result-list UI. Robots intentionally disallows query URLs.
2048 game-detail and embedded-play surface, representing playable game pages and rich metadata.
First-step login/account overlay opened from the header; inspected semantics, field assistance, permission code, and passkey support.
Synthetic invalid route representing HTTP/navigation recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The site uses a fixed dark palette rather than honoring the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The CSS feature probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule and computed color-scheme was normal; light/default and dark-emulated captures use the same dark surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light and dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The rendered CSS/HTML probe found no view-transition usage even though the browser supports document.startViewTransition.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrained same-document and cross-document transitions for card-to-game and route changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: A large consent interstitial obscures the primary content on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots on the home, category, game, and 404 routes show a centered consent wall covering the game grid or active game.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface where legally possible, retain an equally prominent reject action, and avoid repeatedly interrupting navigation.

findings.summary: Consent and login overlays are custom containers rather than semantic dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The feature and login probes found zero dialog and popover elements while visible modal surfaces were present; the login email field had no role=dialog ancestor.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement modal flows with <dialog> and transient UI with popover, including focus management, Escape handling, and declarative dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: The consent dialog does not fit a 360 px viewport and clips its action row.
findings.evidence: The 360×800 search screenshot shows “Agree & Continue” cut off beyond the right edge and the modal consuming almost the whole viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow consent actions into a vertical or wrapping layout at narrow widths and use max-inline-size/min() with safe viewport padding.

findings.summary: Several controls are undersized and some buttons lack a visible programmatic focus treatment.
findings.evidence: The focus probe measured top controls at 40×40, nav links at 59×34, and multiple focused buttons with outline-style none and no box shadow; Lighthouse also failed button-name.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44×44 touch targets and a high-contrast :focus-visible ring on every interactive control.

findings.summary: The homepage misses the good Core Web Vitals range in lab testing.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 3.46 s and CLS 0.578 with a performance score of 0.56; the game detail also measured CLS 0.243.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP card/image, reserve all card and consent dimensions, and delay non-critical hydration and third-party work.

findings.summary: Late layout movement is severe on the homepage and remains poor on game detail.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded CLS 0.578 on home and 0.243 on /game/2048; the image audit found 99 of 100 images without width/height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image and dynamic UI space with width/height or aspect-ratio and prevent consent/banner insertion from moving content.

findings.summary: A very long main-thread task delays responsiveness during load.
findings.evidence: The trace summary found a 1,172.66 ms longest task and 1,173.35 ms total blocking time; Lighthouse reported 3.1 s main-thread work.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the long task, split hydration and card-list work into smaller scheduled chunks, and defer below-fold work.

findings.summary: The initial dependency chain and image delivery are heavier than necessary.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,110 ms render-blocking savings and 2,287 KiB image-delivery savings; the HAR recorded 236 requests and 2.27 MB transferred in its capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, keep deferred scripts deferred, right-size card images, and prioritize only the actual LCP image.

findings.summary: The homepage ships avoidable unused and legacy code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 174 KiB unused JavaScript, 19 KiB unused CSS, and 39 KiB legacy JavaScript on home; game detail showed 465 KiB unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split route-only features, remove legacy transforms for supported browsers, and defer below-fold component code.

findings.summary: Some controls expose invalid or missing accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed aria-prohibited-attr and button-name on the homepage; the DOM recon also found image-only links with empty text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every interactive element a stable accessible name, remove prohibited ARIA, and verify card/link names in the accessibility tree.

findings.summary: Game-detail text includes insufficient color contrast.
findings.evidence: Desktop Lighthouse failed the color-contrast audit on /game/2048.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise muted text and control contrast to WCAG AA while preserving the dark theme hierarchy.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not consistently visible on button controls.
findings.evidence: Programmatically focused header and modal buttons computed to outline-style none with no box shadow; native anchor outlines were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a consistent :focus-visible indicator and test a complete keyboard traversal through header, cards, consent, and login.

findings.summary: Narrow-screen reflow and target sizing are not consistently inclusive.
findings.evidence: At 360×800 the consent actions clip horizontally; several controls measured only 34–40 px high, and Lighthouse failed its viewport scaling audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow full zoom, reflow dialog actions without clipping, and enlarge compact controls to at least 44 CSS px.

findings.summary: Most image elements omit intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 99 of 100 images without width and height attributes; Lighthouse also failed unsized-images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width and height for every image and retain aspect-ratio when CSS scales cards.

findings.summary: Production diagnostics are incomplete and Chrome reports inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed valid-source-maps for large first-party JavaScript and inspector-issues on both representative Lighthouse runs.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish protected production source maps and resolve the specific Chrome Issues-panel warnings in CI.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP is absent and several cookies use weak attributes.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found no Content-Security-Policy; the cookie probe found three non-Secure first-party cookies and all five cookies using SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure; use Lax/Strict unless cross-site delivery is required.

findings.summary: The consent and third-party surface is unusually broad for initial browsing.
findings.evidence: The consent copy states that 1,336 technology partners may process data; the tracker probe observed eight non-page origins and Sentry, while the HAR recorded 230 cross-origin requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce configured consent vendors to those actually used, gate optional analytics until consent, and document each cross-origin dependency.

findings.summary: The account sign-in surface does not expose phishing-resistant passkey authentication.
findings.evidence: The login flow exposed email/password inputs, and a fetched-script probe found no PublicKeyCredential, navigator.credentials create/get, or passkey implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer WebAuthn passkeys alongside recovery methods and request browser permissions only after an explicit user action.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found no Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. HSTS, nosniff, and SAMEORIGIN framing protection were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strict Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, then strengthen HSTS after subdomain readiness review.

findings.summary: The document declares language/direction correctly but CSS remains dominated by physical directional properties.
findings.evidence: The DOM reported lang=en and dir=ltr, while the CSS probe counted 329 physical left/right declarations versus only six logical-property uses.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate spacing, positioning, and sizing to inline/block logical properties and test an RTL locale.

findings.summary: The sign-in password field does not advertise the expected autocomplete purpose.
findings.evidence: The login probe found autocomplete=email on email but an empty autocomplete value on the password input.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=email or username and autocomplete=current-password, preserving password-manager and paste support.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes substantial bytes on the media-heavy homepage.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 2,287 KiB image savings; the image audit found 25 below-fold images without lazy loading, 13 legacy-format images, and 99 missing intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Right-size and modernize thumbnails, lazy-load below-fold media, and keep responsive srcset/sizes aligned with rendered card slots.

findings.summary: Persistent navigation chrome does not adapt to scroll state.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no scroll-state or scroll-driven timeline use; screenshots show a fixed top bar and full-height side rail occupying persistent viewport space.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS scroll-state/container behavior to reduce or adapt persistent chrome while preserving orientation and controls.

Restore production source-map and Issues-panel hygiene
